limitations: One small synthetic TypeScript repository and three query/budget cases; no production or multi-repository latency claim.
Three repetitions per case; nearest-rank p95 equals the maximum observation and is not a confidence interval.
Indexer and memory implementations are frozen equally in both arms; full current application lifecycle changes are outside this isolated timing.
OS page caches were not flushed. Arms alternate by repeat; both run in one Python process on separate cloned databases.
Measured CPU is Python process_time, not sampled whole-machine CPU or memory.
read_source function calls are not exact filesystem I/O counts. All 86 calls remain in both profiled natural requests.
Response equivalence ignores only exact session/retrieval IDs, including embedded next-retrieval references; evidence, hashes, scores, graph, warnings and budgets are otherwise identical.
The earlier nine-request pre-edit diagnostic remains .local/refinement-perf/before.json and is not substituted for the interleaved paired observations.
final_source_scope_note: These timings predate the final focused primary-file selector and ranking refinements. They isolate context/database performance changes with exact measured candidate source snapshots. Running the standalone harness against the final checkout can legitimately report different evidence and failed equivalence; that does not reproduce this historical candidate. Use the linked measured source snapshots when reproducing this stage.
